subject: [FastCart] Canary fallback window - eligibility and postmortem request
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@fastcart.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fastcart.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 16:14:00 -0800
Subject: Checkout failures + high tail latency during canary fallback (urgent)

Hi Connor,

We observed a brief but severe checkout impact this afternoon during your canary fallback. Between 16:10 and 16:24 PST we saw a spike of 503s and very long checkout latencies (some requests hitting >90s). This directly affected our promotions checkout flow — we estimate ~2.8k failed transactions and ~$35k in abandoned carts during the window.

We need two things urgently:
- Confirmation of the exact service window on your side (we have 16:10:12–16:24:08 PST).
- Whether this qualifies under Redwood's availability SLA for credit.

Can you also escalate for an accelerated postmortem? We're preparing a customer-facing impact summary and would like a technical RCA and raw traces attached. I've attached a screenshot of our monitoring and a short list of affected checkout IDs.

Thanks — Nora
Nora Patel
Head of Ops, FastCart
nora.patel@fastcart.com
(415) 555-0199

Attachments: fastcart-503s-screenshot.png (image/png), affected-checkout-ids.csv (text/csv)
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@fastcart.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 16:38:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkout failures + high tail latency during canary fallback (urgent)

Nora —

Thanks for the heads up and the timestamp. I'm sorry this hit FastCart during a promotion window. We are treating this as high priority.

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) I'm pulling the server-side request traces and the canary routing logs now. Expect a raw trace bundle shortly.
2) I've looped in Laura (CS) and Aditya (sales) so we can coordinate SLA/credit conversations and customer comms.
3) Can you confirm the precise list of checkout IDs you want correlated to our traces (if it’s the CSV you attached, we’ll use that)?

Prelim note: the pattern you described (503s during a canary fallback) suggests a routing mismatch where a small set of canary replicas were routed traffic without warmed KV caches. I need the traces to confirm. If that pattern holds, it is likely eligible for a proportional availability credit under our SLA, but I won't finalize until we've reconciled request counts and eligibility windows.

I will share the trace bundle and a summary of the initial telemetry within the hour. For the postmortem, when can you do a 60-minute technical debrief — we can host tomorrow morning PST or later today if needed.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Attachment (outgoing): request for fastcart CSV confirmation
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 17:02:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkout failures + high tail latency during canary fallback (urgent)

Connor / Aditya —

Thanks for the quick loop-in. Operational checklist for evidence to adjudicate an availability credit:
- Raw trace bundle (token-level timing, request -> response) for 16:05–16:30 PST (we need a 20% pre/post buffer).
- Router decision/logs showing canary -> production routing for the same timeframe.
- Tokenization and KV-cache hit rate histograms for canary replicas during the window.
- A count of affected tenant transactions (FastCart tenant id) and deduped failed request IDs.

If FastCart can confirm the CSV, we'll attach it to our telemetry match. Once telemetry is reconciled we can compute a prorated credit (standard formula: time-weighted availability loss * monthly commitment) and present a proposed credit amount for approval.

I suggest we schedule a 30–60 min RCA morning slot tomorrow (09 Dec GMT? — sorry, timezone mixup — I mean tomorrow morning PST) to review the initial findings and confirm any compensatory offers before customer-facing comms. Connor, please include the incident Jira link and Drive folder when you send the traces.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Director, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkout failures + high tail latency during canary fallback (urgent)

Nora —

Attached is the initial telemetry bundle and an evidence packet for the window you reported: 2026-12-09 16:05:00–16:30:00 PST. Files included: fc-traces-20261209-16-10-16-24.zip (raw traces), routing-log-snippet.txt, and a short summary (canary-rca-summary.md).

Prelim findings (high level):
- Canary replicas received ~3.4k checkout requests in the window; approximately 2.7k were retried / surfaced as 5xx at the client due to tokenization/KV warmup misses that cascaded into timeouts.
- The orchestrator route selector sent a higher-than-expected share of production traffic to two new canary pods while their KV caches were cold.
- This matches FastCart's reported times and the majority of the failed transaction IDs in the CSV you provided.

Next steps:
- Laura will calculate tentative proportional credit per our SLA once telemetry reconciliation completes.
- We propose a 60-minute postmortem tomorrow 10:00 PST to walk the traces and confirm mitigation actions (canary warmup changes and routing guardrails). Please confirm if 10:00 PST works or propose a different slot.

Links & docs: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026 (incident), https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-FastCart-Logs

If FastCart approves, we will prepare a formal credit offer and a customer-facing RCA.

—Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: fc-traces-20261209-16-10-16-24.zip (log bundle), routing-log-snippet.txt (text), canary-rca-summary.md (text)
